problem: Open-vocabulary 3D maps such as VLMaps, ConceptFusion and OpenScene store a CLIP-like feature for every point, voxel or cell. They are memory-heavy, have no abstraction above objects, and struggle with large multi-story buildings and hierarchical queries such as 'towel in the bathroom on the upper floor'. Existing 3D scene graphs are either closed-set (Hydra, S-Graphs) or open-vocabulary but limited to small single-room scenes with no floor/room hierarchy and no navigable structure (ConceptGraphs).
motivation: Robots need a compact, object-centric, hierarchical and actionable representation to ground abstract natural-language goals in large indoor environments. The driving observation is that neighbouring 3D points share semantics, so one robust feature per segment can replace dense per-point features. Human-like hierarchies (floor→room→object) let a query be decomposed and matched level by level, which narrows the search space in large buildings.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D scene graph (root→floors→rooms→objects, each carrying CLIP features) from posed RGB-D. Robust segment features come from SAM masks, three-way CLIP fusion and DBSCAN majority features; a multi-floor Voronoi navigation graph is added. LLM-decomposed queries are then grounded level by level and executed by path planning.
insight: Segment-level features are both more accurate and far smaller than dense features when two conditions hold: context-aware CLIP fusion (global frame + crop with background + masked crop without background) and outlier-robust aggregation (DBSCAN majority cluster instead of the mean). In the Replica ablation, removing DBSCAN drops mIoU/F-mIoU from 0.231/0.386 to 0.212/0.340. Using only the background-free masked crop collapses mIoU to 0.136, while the crop with background alone gives 0.215, so context matters most. The hierarchy pays off mainly on large multi-floor scenes and fine-grained queries: it gives +11.69 Retrieval-SR over a floor-augmented ConceptGraphs on object-room-floor queries but only +2.2 on object-room queries. Representing rooms by 10 k-means CLIP view embeddings (73.93% exact accuracy) beats asking GPT-4 to name the room from predicted objects (59.47%), and nearly matches GPT-4 given ground-truth objects on approximate accuracy (84.10 vs 84.25).
method: Frame-wise 3D segment merging: SAM class-agnostic masks per frame are back-projected with depth and odometry into global 3D segments. A fully connected graph is built with edge weight R(m,n)=max(overlap(S_m,S_n), overlap(S_n,S_m)), and highly-connected subgraphs are merged, so one segment can join several existing ones (unlike ConceptGraphs' greedy best-match).

Segment-level CLIP features: per mask, f_i = w_g f_global + w_l f_crop(with background) + w_m f_masked(no background), with weights summing to 1. Features are registered to the nearest points of a reference point cloud and averaged per point. Each segment's point features are then clustered with DBSCAN, and the segment takes the feature closest to the majority-cluster mean.

Floor segmentation: a height histogram (0.01 m bins) is built and peaks within a 0.2 m local range that reach ≥90% of the max peak are kept. DBSCAN groups the peaks and the top-2 per cluster are selected; consecutive heights give floor/ceiling pairs. Each floor node gets a CLIP text embedding of 'floor {#}'.

Room segmentation and view embeddings: per floor, a BEV histogram is thresholded into a wall skeleton, dilated, and turned into a Euclidean distance field whose thresholded regions seed a Watershed segmentation. Each room node stores k=10 k-means CLIP embeddings of the frames whose camera poses lie inside the room. Room type is predicted by max-score or majority vote over the 10 embeddings.

Object nodes: 3D segments are assigned to rooms by BEV overlap, falling back to the nearest room. Overlapping segments that receive the same label are merged. Each object node keeps its point cloud, DBSCAN feature and a max-score label.

Actionable multi-floor Voronoi graph: per-floor free space is (camera-pose region ∪ floor BEV region) minus obstacles with height in [y_min+0.2, y_min+1.5] m, and a Voronoi graph is computed on it. Camera poses on 'stairs' regions form stair graphs that connect to the nearest nodes of the adjacent floor graphs.

Hierarchical language-grounded navigation: few-shot GPT-3.5 parses a query into [floor, room, object]. The target is scored sequentially by CLIP cosine similarity: floor, then room (max over its 10 view embeddings), then object, and a path to it is planned on the Voronoi graph. The supplement adds a particle-filter semantic localization that uses CLIP room and object similarities.

setting.backbone: Frozen foundation models: SAM (masks) + CLIP ViT-H-14 or OVSeg fine-tuned CLIP ViT-L-14 (features) + GPT-3.5 few-shot query parser; classical Voronoi-graph path planning
setting.training_data: none (training-free); relies only on pre-trained SAM, CLIP/OVSeg and GPT-3.5
setting.observation: posed RGB-D sequence (RGB-D + accurate odometry; real world: Azure Kinect RGB-D with FAST-LIO2 LiDAR-SLAM poses), pre-recorded before querying
setting.action_space: path on a multi-floor Voronoi navigation graph to the retrieved target (graph waypoints)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3DSem scenes); offline Replica and ScanNet reconstructions for 3D segmentation
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration: the full map is built beforehand from a recorded RGB-D walk. Accurate/GT odometry is used in simulation. Room-classification evaluation uses GT class-agnostic room masks.

numbers_note: The paper does not evaluate on any standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark. All results are on custom subsets: 8 Replica scenes, 5 ScanNet val scenes, and 8 manually recorded HM3DSem (HM3D val-range 008xx) scenes. The HM3DSem navigation SR is a custom 1 m Euclidean criterion over pre-built maps and has no SPL. Per-scene breakdowns are in supplementary Tables S.1-S.3. A single-scene AUC_k^top of 86.52 (scene 00824) appears only in a figure. The backbone of the HM3DSem retrieval rows is ambiguous: the supplement labels the (o,r,f) row 'w/ OVSeg' while the storage section says ViT-H-14. Ablation rows are omitted here (Replica, no DBSCAN: 0.212/0.340/0.290).
results: On open-vocabulary 3D semantic segmentation, HOV-SG (ViT-H-14) reaches mIoU 0.231 on Replica versus ConceptGraphs' 0.18, and mIoU 0.222 / mAcc 0.431 on ScanNet versus 0.16 / 0.28. On HM3DSem its object-level semantics reach AUC_k^top 84.88, against ConceptGraphs 84.07 and VLMaps 56.20. Its view-embedding room classifier achieves 73.93% exact accuracy, versus 59.47% for GPT-4 given predicted objects. Hierarchical object-room-floor retrieval reaches 28.00% versus 16.31% for a floor-augmented ConceptGraphs, with 37.32% navigation SR in Habitat. The representation is about 75% smaller than VLMaps (1493 vs 6068 MB over 8 scenes). On a real Spot robot in a two-story office it reaches 56.1% object-goal navigation success, 55.6% on room goals and 100% on floor goals.
limitations: The multi-stage pipeline has many hyper-parameters. Construction is slow and offline, not real-time, and requires a pre-recorded exploration with accurate odometry.
It assumes a static environment and cannot handle dynamic scenes.

The heuristic morphological room segmentation fails on open or ambiguous layouts, e.g. combined kitchen-living rooms. CLIP view embeddings confuse visually similar rooms (seminar, meeting and dining rooms), and objects suffer from over- and under-segmentation.
compares_to: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 room classification from object lists
